question: Should OpenClaw core own a hidden host-attested final-capture command and its operation-scoped recovery journal now, or should this lifecycle remain outside core until the RFC assigns durable ownership and compatibility guarantees?
rationale: The patch is intentionally private and technically bounded, but it establishes durable recovery and closure-attestation semantics that cannot be selected safely from code review alone.

options.title: Accept the private core slice
options.body: Approve the RFC ownership split, including host-attestation limits, canonical inventory ownership, journal lifecycle, and the conditions for promoting the command beyond private use.

options.title: Pause for RFC ownership decision
options.body: Keep this stacked PR open but do not merge until an authorized owner accepts the host/core boundary and the durable journal's upgrade contract.

options.title: Move capture orchestration to the host
options.body: Keep only generic snapshot capabilities in core and have the external recovery host own closure evidence, orchestration, and journaling.

recommendation.title: Pause for RFC ownership decision
recommendation.body: Keep this stacked PR open but do not merge until an authorized owner accepts the host/core boundary and the durable journal's upgrade contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor is the identifiable author of the linked RFC-backed stacked recovery design and can provide the precise proposal context; repository product ownership must still make the final choice.
